quests.instruction: Rice, apples and cheese are all foods we eat. Which one comes from an animal instead of a plant?
quests.hint: Think about who makes the milk it is made from.
quests.explanation: Cheese is made from milk, and milk comes from animals such as cows and goats. Rice and apples grow on plants.
quests.funFact: Plants make their own food from sunlight, but animals have to eat other living things.

quests.instruction: Which tall grass has seeds that are ground into the flour used for most bread?
quests.hint: Its golden stalks wave in big fields.
quests.explanation: The seeds of the wheat plant, called grains, are ground into flour. Lettuce is a leaf and a carrot is a root.
quests.funFact: Wheat is one of the most widely grown crops in the world.

quests.instruction: In an orchard, pickers reach up to harvest fruit from tall trees. Which of these grows in an orchard?
quests.hint: Ladders help the pickers reach the top branches.
quests.explanation: Apples grow on trees, which is why they are picked in orchards. Strawberries grow on low plants and carrots grow underground.
quests.funFact: An apple tree grown from a seed can take several years before it bears fruit.

quests.instruction: Which farm animal gives us the milk we drink?
quests.hint: A farmer milks her morning and evening.
quests.explanation: Dairy cows give milk. Hens lay eggs and pigs are raised for meat.
quests.funFact: A dairy cow starts giving milk after she has had a calf.

quests.instruction: A plant has roots, leaves and flowers. Which of these foods is a root?
quests.hint: It grows under the soil, topped by feathery leaves.
quests.explanation: The carrot is the root of its plant. Lettuce is made of leaves and broccoli is a cluster of flower buds.
quests.funFact: Roots hold a plant in the soil and soak up water, and a carrot stores extra sugar in its root.

quests.instruction: A farmer collects eggs from a coop each morning. Which animal laid them?
quests.hint: It sits on a nest of straw.
quests.explanation: Hens are the birds that lay the eggs we eat. Fish live in water and sheep are raised for wool, milk and meat.
quests.funFact: An egg that is kept warm by a hen hatches into a chick after about three weeks.

quests.instruction: Cow's milk is not the only milk used for cheese. Which animal also gives milk that can be made into cheese?
quests.hint: It has a little beard and loves to climb.
quests.explanation: Goats give milk, and many cheeses are made from it. Hens lay eggs and pigs do not give milk for cheese.
quests.funFact: Feta cheese is traditionally made from sheep's milk, sometimes mixed with goat's milk.

quests.instruction: What cooking oil is made by pressing olives?
quests.hint: It is a golden-green liquid.
quests.explanation: Pressing olives squeezes out their oil. Butter is made from cream and honey is made by bees.
quests.funFact: Olive trees can live for hundreds of years.

quests.instruction: Which farm animal grows a thick woolly coat and also gives milk for some cheeses?
quests.hint: Its coat is cut off each spring.
quests.explanation: Sheep grow wool and some are milked for cheese. Cows and goats do not have wool.
quests.funFact: A sheep's wool grows back after it is cut.

quests.instruction: Which list shows how wheat becomes bread, in the right order?
quests.correctAnswer: Wheat grows, flour is ground, bread is baked 🍞
options: Flour is ground, bread is baked, wheat grows 🍞
Bread is baked, wheat grows, flour is ground 🍞
Wheat grows, flour is ground, bread is baked 🍞
quests.hint: Bread cannot be baked before the flour exists.
quests.explanation: Wheat has to grow first, then its grains are ground into flour, and last the flour is baked into bread.
quests.funFact: Wheat grains grow in a head at the top of each stalk.

quests.instruction: Which small insect carries pollen from flower to flower so that fruits can grow?
quests.hint: It also makes honey.
quests.explanation: Bees carry pollen as they visit flowers, and this helps flowers turn into fruit. Ants and ladybugs do not do this job.
quests.funFact: One bee may visit hundreds of flowers in a single day.

quests.instruction: In a vegetable garden, which red food hangs from a plant that is tied to a stake for support?
quests.hint: Its plant has green vines and heavy fruits.
quests.explanation: Tomatoes hang from vines above the ground. Potatoes and carrots grow underground.
quests.funFact: Heavy tomatoes can pull the stems down, so gardeners support the plants with stakes or cages.

quests.instruction: What seasoning can be gathered from seawater after the sun dries the water away?
quests.hint: People collect it from shallow pools by the sea.
quests.explanation: Seawater contains salt. When the water dries up, white salt crystals are left behind.
quests.funFact: Salt is also mined from underground, where ancient seas dried up long ago.

quests.instruction: Which sweet syrup is made by boiling sap collected from maple trees?
quests.hint: Trees are tapped in late winter.
quests.explanation: Maple sap is mostly water. Boiling it removes the water and leaves thick, sweet syrup.
quests.funFact: It takes about forty buckets of maple sap to make one bucket of syrup.

quests.instruction: Which list shows how butter is made, in the right order?
quests.correctAnswer: Cow gives milk, cream is separated, cream is churned 🧈
options: Cream is churned, cow gives milk, cream is separated 🧈
Cream is separated, cream is churned, cow gives milk 🧈
Cow gives milk, cream is separated, cream is churned 🧈
quests.hint: Butter needs cream, and cream needs milk.
quests.explanation: Butter starts as milk from a cow. The cream is taken off the milk and churned until it turns into butter.
quests.funFact: Butter is churned until the fat clumps together and the watery buttermilk is drained off.

quests.instruction: Where is wheat ground into flour?
quests.hint: Heavy stones or rollers crush the grain there.
quests.explanation: A mill grinds grain into flour. A bakery bakes the flour into bread and an orchard is where fruit trees grow.
quests.funFact: Old windmills and watermills used moving air or water to turn the grinding stones.

quests.instruction: Which two things from the sky do farmers' crops need to grow?
quests.hint: Plants need light and a drink.
quests.explanation: Plants use sunlight to make food, and rain gives them the water they need. Too much snow, wind or frost can harm crops.
quests.funFact: Farmers sometimes bring water to crops through pipes when there is not enough rain, which is called irrigation.

quests.instruction: Which building has glass walls that keep plants warm so they can grow even in cool weather?
quests.hint: Sunlight shines in through its glass.
quests.explanation: A greenhouse lets sunlight in and holds the warmth. A bakery is for bread and a barn shelters animals and equipment.
quests.funFact: Glass traps warmth, so tomatoes and peppers can grow in a greenhouse in places that are too cool outside.

quests.instruction: A farmer puts something small into the soil to grow a new crop of beans. What is it?
quests.hint: Inside it is a tiny new plant waiting for water.
quests.explanation: A seed holds a tiny plant and some food to start it growing. Flour is ground grain and a leaf is a part of a grown plant.
quests.funFact: A bean seed swells when it takes in water, then cracks open and sends out a root.

quests.instruction: Who bakes loaves of bread and pastries in a bakery?
quests.hint: They often start work before sunrise.
quests.explanation: A baker turns dough into bread. A farmer grows crops and a fisher catches fish.
quests.funFact: Many bakers start work in the early hours so the bread is fresh when the shop opens.

quests.instruction: Who catches fish from rivers, lakes and the sea?
quests.hint: They use nets, lines or traps.
quests.explanation: A fisher catches fish. A beekeeper looks after bees and a farmer grows crops or raises animals.
quests.funFact: Rivers and lakes give us freshwater fish, and the ocean gives us saltwater fish.

quests.instruction: Which list shows how a plant grows, in the right order?
quests.hint: It begins tiny and ends with something to eat.
quests.explanation: A seed sprouts, grows into a plant and then makes fruit, which holds new seeds.
quests.funFact: Fruit is the way many plants carry their seeds to new places.

quests.instruction: Who takes care of beehives and collects honey?
quests.hint: Protective clothing keeps them safe from stings.
quests.explanation: A beekeeper looks after honey bees and gathers the honey. A baker makes bread and a fisher catches fish.
quests.funFact: One hive of honey bees can hold tens of thousands of bees.

quests.instruction: Which snack is taken from the center of a big yellow flower?
quests.hint: The flower turns to face the sun.
quests.explanation: Sunflower seeds grow in the middle of the flower head. Peanuts grow underground and popcorn comes from corn.
quests.funFact: Young sunflowers turn their faces toward the sun as it moves across the sky.

quests.instruction: Who plants crops, looks after them as they grow and harvests them?
quests.hint: They spend much of the day outdoors.
quests.explanation: A farmer grows and harvests crops. A baker bakes and a beekeeper looks after bees.
quests.funFact: Farmers watch the seasons and the weather to decide when to plant.

quests.instruction: Eggs, cheese and honey all come from animals. Which one comes from an insect?
quests.hint: It starts as nectar from flowers.
quests.explanation: Honey is made by bees, which are insects. Eggs come from birds like hens and cheese comes from the milk of mammals.
quests.funFact: A worker bee makes only a tiny amount of honey in her whole life.

quests.instruction: Which list shows how milk gets from the farm to the shop, in the right order?
quests.correctAnswer: Cow is milked, milk is bottled, milk is sold at the shop 🥛
options: Milk is sold at the shop, cow is milked, milk is bottled 🥛
Cow is milked, milk is bottled, milk is sold at the shop 🥛
Milk is bottled, milk is sold at the shop, cow is milked 🥛
quests.hint: Ask yourself what must happen before a bottle can be sold.
quests.explanation: The cow has to be milked first, then the milk is bottled, and then it can be sold in the shop.
quests.funFact: Milk is kept cold on its journey from the farm so that it stays fresh.

quests.instruction: Clues: it grows underground, it is a root, and its orange flesh turns sweet when baked. Which food is it?
quests.hint: You would have to dig for it in the soil.
quests.explanation: A sweet potato is a root that grows underground. A pumpkin grows on a vine and a pear grows on a tree.
quests.funFact: Sweet potatoes come in orange, white and purple types.

quests.instruction: Which liquid food comes from an animal?
quests.hint: Remember the farm animals you have met.
quests.explanation: Milk comes from animals such as cows. Olive oil comes from olives and juice comes from fruit.
quests.funFact: Mammals make milk to feed their babies.

quests.instruction: What food comes from a hen instead of a cow?
quests.hint: It comes in a shell.
quests.explanation: An egg is laid by a hen. Milk and cheese both start with milk from cows.
quests.funFact: An eggshell has thousands of tiny holes that let air pass in and out.
